script: [serious] NASA launched a one-and-a-half-billion-dollar telescope with a mirror ground to the wrong shape. And a test had already shown it. April 1990. The Hubble Space Telescope reached orbit, promising the sharpest pictures of the universe ever taken. Two months later, the first images came back. Blurry. Every star wrapped in a fuzzy halo. The main mirror was too flat at its edges, by about one-fiftieth the width of a human hair. It was enough to ruin everything. The cause was a measuring device used to guide the polishing. One of its lenses was in the wrong place. So the mirror came out perfectly smooth, and perfectly wrong. A second testing device had actually shown the error. Its results were overruled. The team trusted the main device, and assumed the mirror was fine. A senator called Hubble a techno-turkey. In December 1993, astronauts flew up and gave it glasses, a set of corrective mirrors. The new pictures were stunning. Send this to someone who thinks a second opinion is a waste of time. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number fifty-three. A new file every day.
